newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi Air to make announcement about future - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Air to make announcement about future - paper.

text.p: Financially troubled Kiwi International Airlines was expected to make an announcement about its future at noon (0000 GMT), the Waikato Times newspaper reported on Monday.
Kiwi was not immediately available to comment.
There has been growing concern in the past week that the two-year-old trans-Tasman airline may not be able to survive, the paper said.

Kiwi has encountered strong competition, mechanical breakdowns, disruption from the eruption of New Zealand's Mount Ruapehu volcano and other setbacks. Last month Chief Executive Ewan Wilson said more than a third of the 250 staff were being made redundant in restructuring moves.
The Waikato Times said Companies Office investigators began a probe into the airline's financial records at the weekend.
The Times said today's announcement follows a meeting of Kiwi management with its legal and financial advisory team on Sunday afternoon.
Kiwi is due back in the Queensland Supreme Court on Thursday over a disputed debt with the Singapore operators of its leased Airbus.
Region Air grounded the aircraft over the dispute late last month but the court ordered the jet to be released to Kiwi until Thursday.
Kiwi needed at least $1 million to make another lease payment on the aircraft this month, the paper said.
Last week it said it planned to sue Region Air for millions of dollars in damages.
The Times said it understood Kiwi was given a Friday deadline by some of its creditors. The airline began as a trans-Tasman once-a-week charterer two years ago.
